- ## mayafuni *—* 2026/3/24 07:57

  One simple error to fix for one is the amount of times you shoot at an enemy who's not looking at you and then whiff. This one is just a matter of taking your time with your shots tbh.  There's also the fact that after you lose peeker's advantage, you still go for the fast peeks into a fight which isn't exactly the best. There's a video I can link that breaks it down, but basically, once you lose your peeker's advantage, the fight actually shifts to the holder's favor, so you have to work around it. The simplest way to do that is get him to try to swing you OR slice the pie - Example: 2:41 (here is a really good way you sliced the pie here.) Brim is holding you tightly and you've lost your initial advantage, so you slowly cut the angles and then instantly dome him, it's perfect. These are the timestamps you take a raw fight after losing peeker's advantage and get demolished because they just read the swing. (The criteria is AFTER you've peeked and missed, you just swing instantly again) 0:33 1:09 1:47 (though you both whiffed a lot here lol) 2:01 2:16 I think your dueling mechanics are actually fine, your movement is simple, and your adjustments are *decent*, but that will naturally improve over time. I think the only actual thing you should really focus on is being a bit more smart in your duels. It's one thing to be good at duels, but it's easier on yourself to be smarter at taking them, deciding when to slice a pie and when to go for wider swings. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d7ALVT9hYtY (This video really breaks it down way better than whatever I said lol)

Your crosshair placement is way better in dm's as well as how you peek. We see your diagonal peeks bleed through a little, but its really not that bad here. If you were peeking like this in your comp matches thatd be amazing. One thing you struggle with is still crosshair placement especially when there's lateral movements up and down. Focus on having your crosshair at the correct place and if you peek a corner and your crosshair is at a wall, then repeek and make sure it's headheight and where an enemy could be.  You're doing well in dm's compared to the comp match. Your focus should be crosshair placement, and how you peek. Try to do it like it's a dm match, going for duels and being a bit more aggressive would make it faster. Take duels, focus on mechs.

- ## Jay *—* 2025/9/23 20:59

  I watched your VOD and overall there isn’t too much to criticize, but there are a few areas you can improve. Your peeking is a bit weak and sometimes you could be more confident when taking space. For example in A Main when Breach stunned you had the chance to prime dash and push through. It wasn’t a huge mistake to hold back, but those are the kinds of plays that can open rounds. Your ability usage is fine, though I noticed you throw a lot of panic smokes. That’s not the end of the world, but I did notice you don’t use your smokes much to help your team. A clear example was Round 7 where you could have smoked for Sova so he could defuse safely. Right now your gameplay leans a little selfish, which helps your KD but will hurt your team’s chances of winning rounds. Your economy could also use some work. Buying a Sheriff second round is risky since it usually forces you into a weaker buy on the enemy bonus. Sometimes a Sheriff can win an eco, but it is not very consistent. Since you are playing Jett, I think you should practice with the Outlaw and make it part of your second round or half-buy options because it gives you a lot more value. Finally, your minimap awareness is inconsistent. In Round 16 Brim rotated and you and phoenix sat on your thumbs for a tad too long  as much as brim shouldnt have rotated you need to be aware of the spikes location...

- ## Jay *—* 2025/6/24 16:44

  Example: Round 13 — you had a choice to either push with your team or lurk back toward C. In this case, pushing was the right call since your Brim had the lurk — but it’s important to consider that decision every round. There were also a couple rounds where you didn’t buy with your team. It worked out sometimes (you won a few), and it fixed your teams econ, but in general, it's not great to break team buy tempo — especially as an anchor/support agent. Side note — Round 16 was AMAZING. You used your minimap perfectly and peeked only when the enemies were turned. Loved that. Smart, clean play. That said, I’m 50% sure you don’t know any Cypher setups — and look, I’m not a Cypher main sp i honestly dont know.  But if you want free elo, learning just 2–3 strong setups per site will change your game completely. Your awareness needs some work. A lot of small situations could’ve gone your way if you kept your eye on the minimap more. Round 20 is a great example — Reyna clearly suspected Omen could be main. You even watched her check it… and then didn’t check it yourself. Tut tut. Last thing: Use your cages like Jett smokes. They’re super fast and cheap — perfect for splitting up sightlines, stalling a push, letting your team rotate, or creating one-way duels. You left a lot of value on the table by not using them enough. Some rounds could’ve been way easier with just a single well-placed cage.

  Hey  @CyanAngel how's it going - Heres my tracker - https://tracker.gg/valorant/profile/riot/BigGujja%233D2Y/performance?platform=pc&playlist=competitive&season=aef237a0-494d-3a14-a1c8-ec8de84e309c - currently immo1 and was immo2 123 RR earlier this act, and as you'll see I pretty much only play controller (omen, astra, viper, clove) Sorry in advance if I am a bit harsh in this, first time I am reviewing a vod and am just sharing my thoughts. - ## Supersteve1233 [VAL], *—* 2025/5/18 00:14

  Recommendations:

  1. Learn to smoke while running, and not be so exact on your smokes. Timing on a site hit is just as important as the smokes itself.
  2. Mix up your plays more. I'm not asking you to have an insane 100 move playbook, but if you do the same thing every time you hit a site, eventually your enemies will figure it out and just counter it. You don't want to adapt after you get burned, you want to adapt before.
  3. Your crosshair placement tends to be a bit weird when you're moving, it spends a lot of time floating or hugs a bit too close to the wall. You mostly want your crosshair in the wall only when about to peek, before that you want it a bit off the wall.

  And a bonus one: Don't over-respect a sentinel when attacking, especially if you know they're stacking the rest of the map. They have lots of counters, and more accurately they count as 1.5 players (not exact but you get the idea), as long as you're thinking about how to deal with one. Every agent has a way to make it harder for a sentinel to get kills, whether it's breaking trips, moving past them, flashing the senti, droning the trips, mollying the areas they like to play, suppressing the senti, or more.
